summary: The agent completed a substantial implementation, but both suites failed: baseline generated-source fixtures regressed because a common collection wrapper always consumed an extra variable name, and the new suite exposed that object factories did not retain precedence for stream-to-collection mappings.
quick_failure_summary: Existing generated mapper output changed unexpectedly, and stream mappings used the configured collection class instead of the applicable object factory.

details.reasoning: The baseline JUnit report records 26 failures in Issue913SetterMapperForCollectionsTest. Every failure is a generated-source fixture mismatch where an existing local such as `set` became `set1`. The agent added `decoratedAssignment.createUniqueVarName(...)` unconditionally to SetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMapsWithNullCheck, a shared wrapper used even when no configured implementation applies, so its change perturbed existing code generation. This is a regression in agent-modified production code. Separately, the new suite ran 53 tests and failed two compiler variants of shouldGiveObjectFactoriesPrecedenceForStreams: the result was ChosenList instead of FactoryList. The prompt explicitly required that collection results materialized from streams follow the rule and that an applicable object factory still wins, but the agent did not make the stream template account for factory construction. The reference solution does so in StreamMappingMethod.ftl.
details.secondary_factors: The implementation otherwise covered most of the feature: 51 of 53 new tests passed, including configuration parsing, validation, deferred generated types, direct property copies, and configured stream construction. The agent's targeted 140-test regression slice did not include Issue913, and its object-factory test did not cover streams despite the explicit prompt requirement.

problem_assessment.notes: This is a broad annotation-processor feature spanning resource loading, Java-properties semantics, type-system validation, multi-round processing, construction templates, factories, streams, and direct property mappings. The two observed defects were reasonably knowable from the prompt and visible architecture: object-factory precedence for streams was explicit, and preserving unchanged generated output without configuration is a standard regression expectation. The human reference solution demonstrates the task is solvable without relying on hidden conventions.

evidence: The trajectory shows successful processor compilation, processor verification, licensing, checkstyle, a manual multi-round javac validation, and a 140-test focused collection/map/stream regression slice.
The agent encountered a missing apply_patch helper early, but immediately used available editing alternatives and completed a large implementation; this did not prevent coding or validation.

JUnit failures occur after compilation and directly exercise agent-modified collection-generation paths rather than failing in bootstrap, dependency resolution, shared setup, or an unrelated runtime component.

Baseline fixture mismatches correspond directly to the unconditional unique-variable allocation added in SetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMapsWithNullCheck, while the new failures correspond to the omitted stream factory-precedence integration.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful environment or verifier blocker was found; broaden regression coverage to shared collection wrappers and add an explicit stream object-factory precedence test.
